text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 2.2% today, extending a sharp two-week decline, as crude oil prices dropped more than 7% on Monday following news of U.S.–Iran peace talk efforts ahead of the midterm elections. Lower oil prices directly pressure refiner profits: when the raw material (crude) gets cheaper faster than refined products like gasoline and diesel can, the margin refiners earn on each barrel shrinks. The company also disclosed a leadership change and company update on October 29th, which may have added uncertainty as investors awaited details.

The broader headwind is the shift in market sentiment around geopolitical risk. Oil had been elevated partly due to Mideast tensions; talk of diplomatic resolution removes that premium from crude prices. For a refiner like Marathon, this is a double-edged outcome—cheaper crude is good for costs, but the market fears that sustained lower prices and the prospect of peace could mean weaker energy demand and profitability ahead, especially as earnings season unfolds and guidance becomes the focal point for investors.
